title: Consumption adjustment with mean-reverting risk premia: A singular stochastic control approach
summary: We study a two-sided singular stochastic control problem in which changes in consumption carry utility costs and the risk premium follows the mean-reverting Kim-Omberg model. Optimal consumption is reflected between two moving barriers given by thresholds that depend on the current risk premium. These thresholds are the stopping boundaries of a Dynkin game for a two-dimensional diffusion driven by a single Brownian motion.
